title: Which has more area, a rectangle or a parallelogram with equal sides?
description: A rectangle and a parallelogram both have sides of five and four centimetres. Placed on the same base, the rectangle has height four, while the leaning parallelogram has a shorter height, so its area is smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: a parallelogram with the same sides as a rectangle has a shorter height, so a smaller area. Watch for students who think equal sides mean equal areas.

video_script.why: The child uses area as base times height from the solved example to see that leaning a rectangle shortens its height and shrinks its area.
video_script.substitution: Put both shapes on the same base and compare the heights.
video_script.anchor: the book's rectangle and parallelogram with sides 5 cm and 4 cm
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle has the greater area

final_answer.value: the rectangle has the greater area
final_answer.spoken: the rectangle has the greater area

hold_back: The rectangle has the greater area
maths_rules: rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm: area = 5 × 4 = 20 cm²

parallelogram with sides 5 cm and 4 cm on the base 5 cm: the height is the leg of a right triangle whose slanting side 4 cm is the longest side, so the height is less than 4 cm, or equal when the shape is a rectangle
area = 5 × height < 5 × 4 = 20 cm² for a parallelogram that is not a rectangle
check: a height of 3 cm gives 5 × 3 = 15 cm², less than 20 cm²
video_script.design: One rectangle and one leaning parallelogram on the same base. The height settles the comparison.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the rectangle has the greater area
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The rectangle has the greater area.
A leaning parallelogram with the same sides has a smaller area.
